name: GO Classes CS | DS | Asymptotic Notation & Loop Time Complexity | Weekly Quiz 1

question.text:
Consider a problem: Given an array, check whether the array is in sorted order or not. Suppose both iterative and recursive approaches are used to solve this problem.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

  1. Recursive approach gives space complexity as $O(n)$ for recursive stack space.
  2. Iterative approach gives Auxiliary space as $\Theta(n).$
  3. Time Complexity for recursive approach is $O(n).$
  4. Time Complexity for iterative approach is $\Theta(n \log n).$

Rank the following functions by increasing order of growth. That is, find any arrangement $g 1, g 2, g 3, g 4$ of the functions satisfying $g 1=O(g 2), g 2=O(g 3), g 3=$ $\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g} 4)$.
$$
\begin{aligned}
&f_{1}(n)=2^{(\log n)^{4}}
&f_{2}(n)=\pi^{n}
&f_{3}(n)=n^{5(\log n)^{2}}
&f_{4}(n)=\sqrt{2^{\sqrt{n}}}
\end{aligned}
$$

  1. $f 1, f 3, f 4, f 2$
  2. $f 3, f 1, f 4, f 2$
  3. $f 1, f 3, f 2, f 4$
  4. $f 1, f 3, f 4, f 2$

Let $\text{S}_{1}= \displaystyle{}\sum_{r=0}^{\log n-1} \frac{n r}{2^{r}}$, and $\text{S}_{2} = \displaystyle{} \sum_{r=0}^{\log n-1} r 2^{r}$.
Which of the following is true?

  1. $\text{S}_{1}=\Theta(n \log n), \text{S}_{2}=\Theta(n \log n)$
  2. $\text{S}_{1}=\Theta(n), \text{S}_{2}=\Theta(n \log n)$
  3. $\text{S}_{1}=\Theta(n \log n), \text{S}_{2}=\Theta(n)$
  4. $\text{S}_{1}=\Theta(n), \text{S}_{2}=\Theta(n)$

Which of the following(s) is/are correct?

  1. If $f(n)=n \log n, g(n)=\displaystyle{}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{n}{i}$ then $f(n)=\Theta(g(n))$
  2. If $f(n)=1.01^{n}, g(n)=n^{1000}$ then $f(n)=\Omega(g(n))$
  3. If $f(n)=\displaystyle{}\sum_{i=1}^{n} i^{2}, g(n)=n^{3}+\sum_{i=1}^{n} i$ then $f(n)=\Theta(g(n))$
  4. If $f(n)=n !, g(n)=3^{n} \times 5^{n}$ then $f(n)=\Omega(g(n))$

Assume you have two positive functions $f$ and $g$ such that $f(n)$ is in $O(g(n))$. For each of the following statements, decide which one(s) is/are always TRUE.

  1. $2^{f(n)}$ is $O\left(2^{g(n)}\right)$
  2. $f(n)^{2}$ is $O\left(g(n)^{2}\right)$
  3. $f(n)=O\left((f(n))^{2}\right)$
  4. $g(n)=\Omega(g(n))$

Which of the following statement is FALSE?

  1. If $f(n)=\mathcal{O}(g(n))$ and $f(n)=\Omega(g(n))$, then we have $(f(n))^{2}= \Theta\left((g(n))^{2}\right)$
  2. If $f(n)=\mathcal{O}(g(n))$ and $f(n)=\Omega(g(n))$, then we have $f(n)=g(n)$
  3. $2^{n}+n^{2}=\mathcal{O}\left(3^{n}\right)$
  4. $2^{n}+n^{2}=\mathcal{O}\left(2^{n}\right)$

Consider functions $f()$ and $g()$ which are positive increasing functions.

Which of the following(s) is/are correct?

  1. If $f(n)=o(g(n))$ then $\log (f(n))=o(\log (g(n))$, here $o$ is small-oh
  2. If $f(n)=\mathrm{O}(g(n))$ then $e^{f(n)}=\mathrm{O}\left(e^{g(n)}\right)$, here $\mathrm{O}$ is big-oh
  3. If $f(n)=O(g(n))$ then $\log (f(n))=O(\log (g(n))$, here $O$ is big-oh
  4. If $f(n)=o(g(n))$ then $e^{f(n)}=o\left(e^{g(n)}\right)$, here $o$ is small-oh

Determine the complexity of the following code, using “$\Theta$” as indicated.

int sum = 0;
for (int i = 1; i <= n; i *= 2)
    for (int j = 1; j <= i; j++)
        sum++;
        print(sum);
  1. $\Theta \left(n^{2}\right)$
  2. $\Theta\left(n^{2} \log n\right)$
  3. $\Theta(n)$
  4. None of these

What will be the time complexity of $\text{function()}?$

function(int n) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = i; j < i * i; j++) {
            if (j % i == 0) {
                for (int k = 0; k < j; k++) {
                    printf("*");
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
  1. $\Theta \left(n^{3}\right)$
  2. $\Theta\left(n^{4}\right)$
  3. $\Theta\left(n^{5}\right)$
  4. $\Theta\left(n^{2} \log n\right)$

Match Column A with Column B. Column B represents asymptotic time complexity of loops in Column A
